L0.description: Existing 128 cargo tests as the executed baseline.

L1.description: Review findings: COR-001 is resolved by the CHG-001 documentation amendment; PRF-001 functional behavior is covered by existing SSE tests.

L2.description: Diagnosis gaps are assessed explicitly: anonymous arena ownership needs heap symbols/stacks, and the memory delta needs a controlled release A/B. Neither is suitable for a generated deterministic cargo test.

L3.description: No E2E scenario is required for the two review findings.

scenarios.name: Existing 128-test cargo baseline
scenarios.description: Execute the full existing xhm-desktop cargo suite. Product source and existing tests remain read-only.
test_cases: cargo test -p xhm-desktop -> 128 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

scenarios.name: COR-001 documentation threshold amendment
scenarios.description: The stale <10 MiB P2 Done text now states <40 MiB and records the CHG-001 rationale. This resolves the documentation contradiction and does not create an executable Rust behavior contract.
test_cases: P2 Done states Private Bytes <40 MiB and preserves amendment rationale

scenarios.name: PRF-001 Tokio optimization functional regression coverage
scenarios.description: Existing deterministic SSE tests cover connection lifecycle, resubscribe, retry timing and budget reset, and cancellation under header wait and channel backpressure. The freshly executed 128-test baseline includes all of them.

scenarios.name: Anonymous allocation ownership diagnosis gap
scenarios.description: Exact ownership of large anonymous MEM_PRIVATE arenas remains inferred. Heap symbols/stacks are needed; generating a unit test would fabricate attribution rather than verify behavior.
test_cases: Record the ownership gap without fabricated per-component MiB values

expected.behavior: gap is accurately bounded and not converted into a false test

scenarios.name: Controlled runtime-only memory A/B gap
scenarios.description: The +2.535 MiB post-repair delta remains unexplained because no controlled runtime-only A/B exists. This needs a Windows release-process benchmark, not a deterministic cargo unit test.
test_cases: Do not claim memory reduction; retain the diagnostic gap while checking functional convergence

expected.behavior: coverage assessment is honest and no false regression test is generated

coverage_assessment.reason: COR-001 is documentation-only and resolved; PRF-001's functional regression surface is already exercised by the existing SSE tests included in the 128-test cargo baseline. Memory reduction itself is not proven and is not reported as proven.
